NKJV.1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
NKJV.2: “Speak to Aaron and his sons, that they separate themselves from the holy things of the children of Israel, and that they do not profane My holy name by what they dedicate to Me: I am the LORD.
NKJV.3: Say to them: ‘Whoever of all your descendants throughout your generations, who goes near the holy things which the children of Israel dedicate to the LORD, while he has uncleanness upon him, that person shall be cut off from My presence: I am the LORD.
NKJV.4: ‘Whatever man of the descendants of Aaron, who is a leper or has a discharge, shall not eat the holy offerings until he is clean. And whoever touches anything made unclean by a corpse, or a man who has had an emission of semen,
NKJV.5: or whoever touches any creeping thing by which he would be made unclean, or any person by whom he would become unclean, whatever his uncleanness may be—
NKJV.6: the person who has touched any such thing shall be unclean until evening, and shall not eat the holy offerings unless he washes his body with water.
NKJV.7: And when the sun goes down he shall be clean; and afterward he may eat the holy offerings, because it is his food.
NKJV.8: Whatever dies naturally or is torn by beasts he shall not eat, to defile himself with it: I am the LORD.
NKJV.9: ‘They shall therefore keep My ordinance, lest they bear sin for it and die thereby, if they profane it: I the LORD sanctify them.
NKJV.10: ‘No outsider shall eat the holy offering; one who dwells with the priest, or a hired servant, shall not eat the holy thing.
NKJV.11: But if the priest buys a person with his money, he may eat it; and one who is born in his house may eat his food.
NKJV.12: If the priest’s daughter is married to an outsider, she may not eat of the holy offerings.
NKJV.13: But if the priest’s daughter is a widow or divorced, and has no child, and has returned to her father’s house as in her youth, she may eat her father’s food; but no outsider shall eat it.
NKJV.14: ‘And if a man eats the holy offering unintentionally, then he shall restore a holy offering to the priest, and add one-fifth to it.
NKJV.15: They shall not profane the holy offerings of the children of Israel, which they offer to the LORD,
NKJV.16: or allow them to bear the guilt of trespass when they eat their holy offerings; for I the LORD sanctify them.’ ”
NKJV.17: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
NKJV.18: “Speak to Aaron and his sons, and to all the children of Israel, and say to them: ‘Whatever man of the house of Israel, or of the strangers in Israel, who offers his sacrifice for any of his vows or for any of his freewill offerings, which they offer to the LORD as a burnt offering—
NKJV.19: you shall offer of your own free will a male without blemish from the cattle, from the sheep, or from the goats.
NKJV.20: Whatever has a defect, you shall not offer, for it shall not be acceptable on your behalf.
NKJV.21: And whoever offers a sacrifice of a peace offering to the LORD, to fulfill his vow, or a freewill offering from the cattle or the sheep, it must be perfect to be accepted; there shall be no defect in it.
NKJV.22: Those that are blind or broken or maimed, or have an ulcer or eczema or scabs, you shall not offer to the LORD, nor make an offering by fire of them on the altar to the LORD.
NKJV.23: Either a bull or a lamb that has any limb too long or too short you may offer as a freewill offering, but for a vow it shall not be accepted.
NKJV.24: ‘You shall not offer to the LORD what is bruised or crushed, or torn or cut; nor shall you make any offering of them in your land.
NKJV.25: Nor from a foreigner’s hand shall you offer any of these as the bread of your God, because their corruption is in them, and defects are in them. They shall not be accepted on your behalf.’ ”
NKJV.26: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
NKJV.27: “When a bull or a sheep or a goat is born, it shall be seven days with its mother; and from the eighth day and thereafter it shall be accepted as an offering made by fire to the LORD.
NKJV.28: Whether it is a cow or ewe, do not kill both her and her young on the same day.
NKJV.29: And when you offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving to the LORD, offer it of your own free will.
NKJV.30: On the same day it shall be eaten; you shall leave none of it until morning: I am the LORD.
NKJV.31: “Therefore you shall keep My commandments, and perform them: I am the LORD.
NKJV.32: You shall not profane My holy name, but I will be hallowed among the children of Israel. I am the LORD who sanctifies you,
NKJV.33: who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God: I am the LORD.”

ESV.1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
ESV.2: “Speak to Aaron and his sons so that they abstain from the holy things of the people of Israel, which they dedicate to me, so that they do not profane my holy name: I am the LORD.
ESV.3: Say to them, ‘If any one of all your offspring throughout your generations approaches the holy things that the people of Israel dedicate to the LORD, while he has an uncleanness, that person shall be cut off from my presence: I am the LORD.
ESV.4: None of the offspring of Aaron who has a leprous disease or a discharge may eat of the holy things until he is clean. Whoever touches anything that is unclean through contact with the dead or a man who has had an emission of semen,
ESV.5: and whoever touches a swarming thing by which he may be made unclean or a person from whom he may take uncleanness, whatever his uncleanness may be —
ESV.6: the person who touches such a thing shall be unclean until the evening and shall not eat of the holy things unless he has bathed his body in water.
ESV.7: When the sun goes down he shall be clean, and afterward he may eat of the holy things, because they are his food.
ESV.8: He shall not eat what dies of itself or is torn by beasts, and so make himself unclean by it: I am the LORD.’
ESV.9: They shall therefore keep my charge, lest they bear sin for it and die thereby when they profane it: I am the LORD who sanctifies them.
ESV.10: “A lay person shall not eat of a holy thing; no foreign guest of the priest or hired worker shall eat of a holy thing,
ESV.11: but if a priest buys a slave  as his property for money, the slave  may eat of it, and anyone born in his house may eat of his food.
ESV.12: If a priest's daughter marries a layman, she shall not eat of the contribution of the holy things.
ESV.13: But if a priest's daughter is widowed or divorced and has no child and returns to her father's house, as in her youth, she may eat of her father's food; yet no lay person shall eat of it.
ESV.14: And if anyone eats of a holy thing unintentionally, he shall add the fifth of its value to it and give the holy thing to the priest.
ESV.15: They shall not profane the holy things of the people of Israel, which they contribute to the LORD,
ESV.16: and so cause them to bear iniquity and guilt, by eating their holy things: for I am the LORD who sanctifies them.”
ESV.17: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
ESV.18: “Speak to Aaron and his sons and all the people of Israel and say to them, When any one of the house of Israel or of the sojourners in Israel presents a burnt offering as his offering, for any of their vows or freewill offerings that they offer to the LORD,
ESV.19: if it is to be accepted for you it shall be a male without blemish, of the bulls or the sheep or the goats.
ESV.20: You shall not offer anything that has a blemish, for it will not be acceptable for you.
ESV.21: And when anyone offers a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering from the herd or from the flock, to be accepted it must be perfect; there shall be no blemish in it.
ESV.22: Animals blind or disabled or mutilated or having a discharge or an itch or scabs you shall not offer to the LORD or give them to the LORD as a food offering on the altar.
ESV.23: You may present a bull or a lamb that has a part too long or too short for a freewill offering, but for a vow offering it cannot be accepted.
ESV.24: Any animal that has its testicles bruised or crushed or torn or cut you shall not offer to the LORD; you shall not do it within your land,
ESV.25: neither shall you offer as the bread of your God any such animals gotten from a foreigner. Since there is a blemish in them, because of their mutilation, they will not be accepted for you.”
ESV.26: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
ESV.27: “When an ox or sheep or goat is born, it shall remain seven days with its mother, and from the eighth day on it shall be acceptable as a food offering to the LORD.
ESV.28: But you shall not kill an ox or a sheep and her young in one day.
ESV.29: And when you sacrifice a sacrifice of thanksgiving to the LORD, you shall sacrifice it so that you may be accepted.
ESV.30: It shall be eaten on the same day; you shall leave none of it until morning: I am the LORD.
ESV.31: “So you shall keep my commandments and do them: I am the LORD.
ESV.32: And you shall not profane my holy name, that I may be sanctified among the people of Israel. I am the LORD who sanctifies you,
ESV.33: who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God: I am the LORD.”

NASB.1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
NASB.2: 'Tell Aaron and his sons to be careful with the holy [gifts] of the sons of Israel, which they dedicate to Me, so as not to profane My holy name; I am the LORD.
NASB.3: 'Say to them, 'If any man among all your descendants throughout your generations approaches the holy [gifts] which the sons of Israel dedicate to the LORD, while he has an uncleanness, that person shall be cut off from before Me; I am the LORD.
NASB.4: 'No man of the descendants of Aaron, who is a leper or who has a discharge, may eat of the holy [gifts] until he is clean. And if one touches anything made unclean by a corpse or if a man has a seminal emission,
NASB.5: or if a man touches any teeming things by which he is made unclean, or any man by whom he is made unclean, whatever his uncleanness;
NASB.6: a person who touches any such shall be unclean until evening, and shall not eat of the holy [gifts] unless he has bathed his body in water.
NASB.7: 'But when the sun sets, he will be clean, and afterward he shall eat of the holy [gifts], for it is his food.
NASB.8: 'He shall not eat [an animal] which dies or is torn [by beasts], becoming unclean by it; I am the LORD.
NASB.9: 'They shall therefore keep My charge, so that they will not bear sin because of it and die thereby because they profane it; I am the LORD who sanctifies them.
NASB.10: 'No layman, however, is to eat the holy [gift]; a sojourner with the priest or a hired man shall not eat of the holy [gift].
NASB.11: 'But if a priest buys a slave as [his] property with his money, that one may eat of it, and those who are born in his house may eat of his food.
NASB.12: 'If a priest's daughter is married to a layman, she shall not eat of the offering of the [gifts].
NASB.13: 'But if a priest's daughter becomes a widow or divorced, and has no child and returns to her father's house as in her youth, she shall eat of her father's food; but no layman shall eat of it.
NASB.14: 'But if a man eats a holy [gift] unintentionally, then he shall add to it a fifth of it and shall give the holy [gift] to the priest.
NASB.15: 'They shall not profane the holy [gifts] of the sons of Israel which they offer to the LORD,
NASB.16: and [so] cause them to bear punishment for guilt by eating their holy [gifts]; for I am the LORD who sanctifies them.''
NASB.17: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
NASB.18: 'Speak to Aaron and to his sons and to all the sons of Israel and say to them, 'Any man of the house of Israel or of the aliens in Israel who presents his offering, whether it is any of their votive or any of their freewill offerings, which they present to the LORD for a burnt offering--
NASB.19: for you to be accepted-- [it must be] a male without defect from the cattle, the sheep, or the goats.
NASB.20: 'Whatever has a defect, you shall not offer, for it will not be accepted for you.
NASB.21: 'When a man offers a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD to fulfill a special vow or for a freewill offering, of the herd or of the flock, it must be perfect to be accepted; there shall be no defect in it.
NASB.22: 'Those [that are] blind or fractured or maimed or having a running sore or eczema or scabs, you shall not offer to the LORD, nor make of them an offering by fire on the altar to the LORD.
NASB.23: 'In respect to an ox or a lamb which has an overgrown or stunted [member], you may present it for a freewill offering, but for a vow it will not be accepted.
NASB.24: 'Also anything [with its testicles] bruised or crushed or torn or cut, you shall not offer to the LORD, or sacrifice in your land,
NASB.25: nor shall you accept any such from the hand of a foreigner for offering as the food of your God; for their corruption is in them, they have a defect, they shall not be accepted for you.''
NASB.26: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
NASB.27: 'When an ox or a sheep or a goat is born, it shall remain seven days with its mother, and from the eighth day on it shall be accepted as a sacrifice of an offering by fire to the LORD.
NASB.28: 'But, [whether] it is an ox or a sheep, you shall not kill [both] it and its young in one day.
NASB.29: 'When you sacrifice a sacrifice of thanksgiving to the LORD, you shall sacrifice it so that you may be accepted.
NASB.30: 'It shall be eaten on the same day, you shall leave none of it until morning; I am the LORD.
NASB.31: 'So you shall keep My commandments, and do them; I am the LORD.
NASB.32: 'You shall not profane My holy name, but I will be sanctified among the sons of Israel; I am the LORD who sanctifies you,
NASB.33: who brought you out from the land of Egypt, to be your God; I am the LORD.'

WEB.2: “Tell Aaron and his sons to separate themselves from the holy things of the children of Israel, which they make holy to me, and that they not profane my holy name. I am Yahweh.
WEB.3: “Tell them, ‘If anyone of all your offspring  throughout your generations approaches the holy things, which the children of Israel make holy to Yahweh, having his uncleanness on him, that soul shall be cut off from before me. I am Yahweh.
WEB.4: “‘Whoever of the offspring  of Aaron is a leper or has an issue; he shall not eat of the holy things, until he is clean. Whoever touches anything that is unclean by the dead, or a man whose offspring  goes from him;
WEB.5: or whoever touches any creeping thing, whereby he may be made unclean, or a man of whom he may take uncleanness, whatever uncleanness he has;
WEB.6: the person that touches any such shall be unclean until the evening, and shall not eat of the holy things, unless he bathe his body in water.
WEB.7: When the sun is down, he shall be clean; and afterward he shall eat of the holy things, because it is his bread.
WEB.8: That which dies of itself, or is torn by animals, he shall not eat, defiling himself by it. I am Yahweh.
WEB.9: “‘They shall therefore follow my requirements, lest they bear sin for it, and die therein, if they profane it. I am Yahweh who sanctifies them.
WEB.10: “‘No stranger shall eat of the holy thing: a foreigner living with the priests, or a hired servant, shall not eat of the holy thing.
WEB.11: But if a priest buys a slave, purchased by his money, he shall eat of it; and such as are born in his house, they shall eat of his bread.
WEB.12: If a priest’s daughter is married to an outsider, she shall not eat of the heave offering of the holy things.
WEB.13: But if a priest’s daughter is a widow, or divorced, and has no child, and has returned to her father’s house, as in her youth, she may eat of her father’s bread: but no stranger shall eat any of it.
WEB.14: “‘If a man eats something holy unwittingly, then he shall add the fifth part of its value to it, and shall give the holy thing to the priest.
WEB.15: The priests shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel, which they offer to Yahweh,

AMP.1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
AMP.2: "Tell Aaron and his sons to be careful with the holy things (offerings, gifts) which the children of Israel dedicate to Me, so that they do not profane My holy name; I am the LORD.
AMP.3: Say to them, 'Any one of your descendants throughout your generations who approaches the holy things which the Israelites dedicate to the LORD, while he is [ceremonially] unclean, that person shall be cut off from My presence and excluded from the sanctuary; I am the LORD.
AMP.4: No man of the descendants of Aaron who is a leper or has a discharge may eat the holy things [the offerings and the showbread] until he is clean. And whoever touches any person or thing made unclean by contact with a corpse or a man who has had a seminal emission,
AMP.5: or whoever touches any crawling thing by which he is made unclean, or any person by whom he is made unclean, whatever it may be,
AMP.6: the person who touches any such thing shall be unclean until evening and shall not eat the holy things unless he has bathed his body in water.
AMP.7: When the sun sets, he will be clean, and afterward he may eat the holy things, for it is his food.
AMP.8: He shall not eat that which dies [of natural causes] or is torn by a predator, becoming unclean by it; I am the LORD.
AMP.9: Therefore the priests shall observe My ordinance, so that they will not bear sin because of it and die if they profane it; I am the LORD who sanctifies them.
AMP.10: 'No layman [that is, someone outside of Aaron's family] is to eat the holy gift [which has been offered to God]; a foreigner residing with the priest or a hired man shall not eat the holy thing.
AMP.11: But if a priest buys a slave as his property with his money, the slave may eat the holy thing, and those who are born in the priest's house; they may eat his food.
AMP.12: If a priest's daughter is married to a layman [one not part of the priestly tribe], she shall not eat the offering of the holy things.
AMP.13: But if a priest's daughter is a widow or divorced, and has no child, and returns to her father's house as in her youth, she shall eat her father's food; but no layman shall eat it.
AMP.14: But if a person unknowingly eats a holy gift [which has been offered to God], then he shall add one-fifth of its value to it and give the holy gift to the priest.
AMP.15: The priests shall not profane the holy things the Israelites offer to the LORD,
AMP.16: and so cause them [by neglect of any essential observance] to bear the punishment of guilt when they eat their holy things; for I am the LORD who sanctifies them.'"
AMP.17: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
AMP.18: "Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites and say to them, 'Any man of the house of Israel or any stranger in Israel who presents his offering, whether to fulfill any of their vows or as any of their freewill (voluntary) offerings which they presented to the LORD as a burnt offering—
AMP.19: so that you may be accepted—it must be a male without blemish from the cattle, the sheep, or the goats.
AMP.20: You shall not offer anything which has a blemish, because it will not be accepted for you.
AMP.21: Whoever offers a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD to fulfill a special vow to the LORD or as a freewill offering from the herd or from the flock, it must be perfect to be accepted; there shall be no blemish in it.
AMP.22: Animals that are blind or fractured or mutilated, or have a sore or a running wound or an itch or scabs, you shall not offer to the LORD nor make an offering of them by fire on the altar to the LORD.
AMP.23: For a freewill offering you may offer either a bull or a lamb which has an overgrown or stunted member (deformity), but for [the payment of] a vow it will not be accepted.
AMP.24: You shall not offer to the LORD any animal which has its testicles bruised or crushed or torn or cut off, or sacrifice it in your land.
AMP.25: Nor shall you offer as the food of your God any such [animals obtained] from a foreigner, because their corruption and blemish makes them unfit; there is a defect in them, they shall not be accepted for you.'"
AMP.26: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
AMP.27: "When a bull or a sheep or a goat is born, it shall remain for seven days with its mother; and after the eighth day it shall be accepted as an offering by fire to the LORD.
AMP.28: And whether [the mother] is a cow or a sheep, you shall not kill both it and its young in one day.
AMP.29: When you sacrifice an offering of thanksgiving to the LORD, you shall sacrifice it so that you may be accepted.
AMP.30: It shall be eaten on the same day; you shall leave none of it until the next morning; I am the LORD.

NET.2: “Tell Aaron and his sons that they must deal respectfully with the holy offerings of the Israelites, which they consecrate to me, so that they do not profane my holy name. I am the LORD.
NET.3: Say to them, ‘Throughout your generations, if any man from all your descendants approaches the holy offerings which the Israelites consecrate to the LORD while he is impure, that person must be cut off from before me. I am the LORD.
NET.4: No man from the descendants of Aaron who is diseased or has a discharge may eat the holy offerings until he becomes clean. The one who touches anything made unclean by contact with a dead person, or a man who has a seminal emission,

NET.6: the person who touches any of these will be unclean until evening and must not eat from the holy offerings unless he has bathed his body in water.

NET.8: He must not eat an animal that has died of natural causes or an animal torn by beasts and thus become unclean by it. I am the LORD.
